conditions: Frontal cutaway of all four chambers with both circulations

phases.Atrial systole: The atria contract (a wave) and top up the ventricles; atrioventricular valves open, semilunar valves shut.
phases.Isovolumetric contraction: Ventricles contract with all four valves shut (S1 at AV closure); pressure rises steeply at constant volume.
phases.Ventricular ejection: LV pressure exceeds aortic (~80 mmHg) and RV exceeds pulmonary pressure; semilunar valves open and the stroke volume is ejected; LV peaks near 120 mmHg.
phases.Isovolumetric relaxation: Ventricles relax with all valves shut; aortic valve closure gives S2 and the dicrotic notch; pressure falls at constant volume (ESV).
phases.Rapid filling: Ventricular pressure falls below atrial; AV valves open and most ventricular filling occurs passively.
phases.Diastasis: Atrial and ventricular pressures nearly equal; slow filling straight from the veins.

parts.RA: Right atrium: receives deoxygenated blood from the venae cavae; contracts in atrial systole.
parts.RV: Right ventricle: pumps into the pulmonary artery at low pressure (~20 mmHg systolic).
parts.LA: Left atrium: receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins; pressure ~5–10 mmHg.
parts.LV: Left ventricle: thick-walled pump into the aorta; pressure 0–120 mmHg, volume ~125 → ~55 mL.
parts.tricuspid: Tricuspid valve: right atrioventricular valve; opens when RA pressure > RV pressure.
parts.pulmonary: Pulmonary valve: right semilunar valve; opens when RV pressure > pulmonary artery pressure.
parts.mitral: Mitral valve: left atrioventricular valve; opens when LA pressure > LV pressure; its closure contributes to S1.
parts.aortic: Aortic valve: left semilunar valve; opens when LV pressure > aortic pressure; its closure contributes to S2.
parts.aorta: Aorta: receives the LV stroke volume; elastic recoil keeps diastolic pressure ~80 mmHg.
parts.pa: Pulmonary trunk and arteries: carry RV output to the lungs.
parts.cavae: Superior and inferior venae cavae: return systemic venous blood to the right atrium.
parts.pveins: Pulmonary veins: return oxygenated blood to the left atrium.

readouts.LAP: Left atrial pressure (a, c and v waves).
readouts.RAP: Right atrial pressure (≈ central venous pressure).
readouts.LVV: Left ventricular volume: end-diastolic volume at its peak, end-systolic volume at its trough.
readouts.SV: Stroke volume = end-diastolic minus end-systolic volume.
readouts.EF: Ejection fraction = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume.
readouts.ecg: Schematic surface ECG on the same clock: P wave starts atrial contraction, QRS just before ventricular contraction, T wave during late ejection.

concepts: Wiggers diagram: pressure and volume against time
pressure gradients open and close the valves
first heart sound (S1) and second heart sound (S2)
end-diastolic volume, end-systolic volume, stroke volume, ejection fraction
